s: Which one of the following methods is specifically suited for biodegradable kitchen, garden and farm waste and produces manure through an aerobic process?
x: Composting is an aerobic treatment method for biodegradable organic waste and produces manure.
tq: Match the disposal method with the waste type and process.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vermicomposting uses earthworms to convert organic waste into vermicompost.
2. Vermicomposting is primarily meant for mixed hazardous waste.
3. It is suitable for household and other organic waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Vermicomposting uses earthworms and is suitable for household and organic waste. It is not a treatment method for mixed hazardous waste.
tq: Identify the wrong statement by checking whether the waste stream suits the method.

s:
Anaerobic digestion of properly segregated organic waste primarily produces which of the following?
1. Methane or biogas
2. Slurry usable as fertiliser
3. Oxygen-rich ash
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Anaerobic digestion produces methane or biogas and a nutrient-rich slurry that can be used as fertiliser. Oxygen-rich ash is not its principal product.
tq: Separate the actual products of anaerobic treatment from those associated with combustion.

s: Why is segregation essential before undertaking anaerobic digestion of municipal waste?
o: It prevents the formation of methane
It ensures that only suitable organic waste enters the digester
It eliminates the need for slurry management
It converts inert waste into combustible fuel
x: Anaerobic digestion is meant for organic waste only; segregation prevents unsuitable materials from entering the process.
tq: Apply the method-to-waste restriction to a practical waste-management situation.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anaerobic digestion — production of biogas and slurry manure
Pyrolysis — heating waste in the presence of abundant oxygen
Incineration — treatment without any ash generation
Sanitary landfill — treatment of all recyclable waste
x: Anaerobic digestion converts segregated organic waste into methane-rich biogas and slurry manure. Pyrolysis occurs without oxygen, incineration produces ash, and sanitary landfills are intended for residual waste.
tq: Use process conditions and end products to reject reversed or absolute pairings.

s: In pyrolysis, mixed or contaminated waste is:
o: Compacted in cells and covered daily with earth
Burnt in open air to recover only metal
Biologically decomposed by earthworms to produce manure
Heated in the absence of oxygen to produce gas, oil and char
x: Pyrolysis heats waste without oxygen and produces gas, oil and char. It is particularly associated with mixed or contaminated waste streams.
tq: Distinguish pyrolysis from aerobic decomposition, landfilling and open burning by its operating condition.

s: Which of the following wastes is most appropriately disposed of in a sanitary landfill?
o: Segregated kitchen waste for biogas production
x: Sanitary landfills are intended only for residual waste that is non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert.
tq: Apply the residual-waste rule instead of treating landfilling as a universal option.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding sanitary landfills:
1. Waste is compacted in cells and covered with earth daily.
2. Liners and leachate-collection systems are used.
3. The method relies mainly on containment rather than treatment.
4. It is intended for all biodegradable waste without segregation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Sanitary landfills use compacted cells, daily cover, liners and leachate collection, and rely on containment. They are not meant for all biodegradable waste without segregation.
tq: Find the single overbroad statement in a group describing a controlled facility.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic monitoring or control measure associated with a sanitary landfill?
o: Mandatory use of earthworms for decomposition
x: Sanitary landfills involve containment, liners, leachate collection, and methane and groundwater monitoring. Earthworms are associated with vermicomposting, not a mandatory landfill measure.
tq: Identify the option borrowed from a different treatment method.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Indore method of composting?
o: Anaerobic pits with alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil for four to six months
Aerobic composting in which organic waste is turned at intervals
Heating mixed waste without oxygen to obtain oil and char
x: The Indore method is aerobic composting in which the material is turned at intervals. The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits with alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil.
tq: Discriminate between the closely associated Indore and Bangalore composting methods.

s: The Bangalore method of composting is characterised by:
o: Turning organic waste at regular intervals in an aerobic system
Using earthworms in household composting units
Converting waste into syngas through plasma
Placing alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil in pits for about four to six months
x: The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits containing alternate layers of municipal solid waste and night soil and generally takes four to six months.
tq: Use the distinctive process and duration to separate the Bangalore method from similar methods.

s: Indore and Bangalore methods of composting were systematised by Howard and developed by:
x: Howard systematised the Indore and Bangalore methods, while Acharya and Subrahmanyam developed them.
tq: Test the specific attribution of a method to its associated persons.

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Waste)
 a. E-waste
 b. Broken glass pieces
 c. Biomedical waste
 d. Non-recyclable high-calorific dry waste

List-II (Preferred method)
 i. Incineration at a common biomedical waste treatment facility
 ii. Recycling
 iii. RDF or co-processing in cement kilns
 iv. Landfilling

option_a: a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
option_b: a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
option_c: a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
option_d: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i
x: E-waste is sent for recycling, broken glass pieces are landfilled, biomedical waste is incinerated at a common biomedical waste treatment facility, and high-calorific dry waste is used as RDF or co-processed in cement kilns.
tq: Start with the sure waste-treatment pairs and eliminate codes containing a wrong pair.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes incineration from pyrolysis?
o: Incineration heats waste in the absence of oxygen, whereas pyrolysis uses excess oxygen
Incineration is controlled high-temperature burning, whereas pyrolysis heats waste without oxygen
Both methods are biological processes using earthworms
Both methods are restricted to inert waste in sanitary landfills
x: Incineration is controlled high-temperature combustion, while pyrolysis is thermal treatment in the absence of oxygen.
tq: Compare the defining operating condition of two similar thermal technologies.

s: Plasma gasification converts waste primarily into:
x: In plasma gasification, plasma converts waste into synthetic fuel, commonly referred to as syngas. Sweden is cited as an example associated with this technology.
tq: Recall the characteristic output of an advanced thermal waste-treatment technology.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Waste-to-energy or RDF is suitable for high-calorific plastic, paper and textile waste.
2. RDF is generally prepared by shredding and drying the waste.
3. RDF can be used as fuel in cement kilns.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: High-calorific plastic, paper and textile waste can be shredded and dried to produce RDF, which may be used as fuel in cement kilns.
tq: Confirm the complete chain from suitable waste to preparation and end use.

s: Legacy waste dumps are generally cleared through:
x: Biomining is used to clear legacy waste dumps by excavating, segregating and processing the accumulated waste.
tq: Associate the specialised remediation term with old accumulated dumps.

s:
With reference to the processing of legacy waste in Ongole, consider the following statements:
1. About 1.76 lakh tonnes out of 2.56 lakh tonnes were processed.
2. The recovered refuse-derived fuel was sent to cement plants.
3. The waste was disposed of entirely through open dumping.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Ongole processed about 1.76 lakh tonnes out of 2.56 lakh tonnes, and its recovered RDF was sent to cement plants. Open dumping was not the stated management route.
tq: Check both the quantitative detail and the stated end use while rejecting the contradictory disposal claim.

s: Which one of the following is an inappropriate statement regarding uncontrolled dumping?
o: It may create risks associated with leachate and uncontrolled emissions.
It lacks the containment measures of a sanitary landfill.
It is the preferred method for residual waste in urban India.
It is not a viable waste-management option.
x: Uncontrolled dumping is not a viable or preferred waste-management option. Sanitary landfilling provides controlled containment for suitable residual waste.
tq: Reject the option that reverses the basic distinction between controlled and uncontrolled disposal.

s:
Arrange the following waste-management methods in the order of the principal treatment condition involved, beginning with aerobic biological treatment:
A. Pyrolysis
B. Composting
C. Anaerobic digestion
D. Incineration
x: Composting is aerobic biological treatment, anaerobic digestion is oxygen-free biological treatment, incineration is combustion, and pyrolysis is heating without oxygen.
tq: Order the methods by their defining treatment conditions rather than by their names.

s: R2 certification is associated with:

Which practices are commonly associated with informal e-waste dismantling?
1. Open burning
2. Acid baths
3. Processing only through certified facilities

x: Informal workers often dismantle e-waste through open burning and acid baths. Processing only through certified facilities is a formal, not informal, practice.
tq: Identify the two hazardous informal practices and reject the formal-system statement.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022?

They replaced the 2016 E-waste Rules and cover only mobile-phone batteries.
They apply only to lead-acid batteries used in automobiles.
They exclude batteries from the EPR framework.

s: Which of the following best expresses the relationship between EPR under the E-waste Rules, 2022 and the circular economy?
o: EPR prohibits the trading of recycling certificates.
EPR links producers with collection, recycling and resource recovery over the product life cycle.
EPR shifts all responsibility for e-waste to local bodies.
EPR permits only informal dismantling of obsolete equipment.

Only centralised collection and unrestricted disposal in landfills

x: The INC venues were Punta del Este, Paris, Nairobi, Ottawa, Busan and Geneva in that order. Busan hosted INC-5 in 2024 and Geneva hosted INC-5.2 in August 2025.
tq: Fix the first and last venues, then arrange the middle venues chronologically.

s:
The INC-5.2 meeting held in Geneva in August 2025 ended with no agreement. Which of the following were identified as major sticking points?
1. Production caps
2. Chemicals of concern
3. Finance
4. Establishment of informal e-waste hubs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Production caps, chemicals of concern and finance were the major sticking points. Informal e-waste hubs were not an issue in the INC negotiations.
tq: Eliminate the statement imported from a neighbouring environmental topic.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, the ban on single-use plastic and carry bags applies to carry bags having thickness below:
x: Andhra Pradesh bans single-use plastic and carry bags below 120 microns, with enforcement involving the Revenue Department, Police and Pollution Control Board.
tq: Distinguish the precise statutory threshold from nearby thickness values.

s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the action reported under Andhra Pradesh plastic curbs during AP SES 2025–26?
o: 3,571.40 tonnes carry bags and 5,505.06 tonnes single-use plastic seized
3,571.40 kg carry bags and 5,505.06 kg single-use plastic seized
5,505.06 tonnes carry bags and 3,571.40 tonnes single-use plastic seized
5,505.06 kg carry bags and 3,571.40 kg single-use plastic seized
x: The reported seizures were 5,505.06 kg of carry bags and 3,571.40 kg of single-use plastic.
tq: Check both the units and the order of the two figures.

s:
With reference to the plastic curbs in Guntur, consider the following statements:
1. A complete ban was scheduled from 15 August 2026.
2. Fines could extend up to ₹5,000.
3. Fines were to be collected through the Swachh App.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: Guntur’s complete ban was scheduled from 15 August 2026, fines could reach ₹5,000, and the Swachh App was to be used for fines.
tq: Verify the date, monetary limit and enforcement mechanism separately.

s: Which of the following best defines e-waste in the context of the ITU definition?
o: Only hazardous electronic equipment exported across borders
Only discarded computers sent for recycling
All household waste containing any metal component
Discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts not meant for reuse
x: E-waste consists of discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts that are not intended for reuse.
tq: Prefer the definition covering both equipment and parts, and excluding items meant for reuse.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a hazardous constituent released by old computers?
x: Old computers can release beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury and lead, besides PCBs and PBBs. Plutonium is not included in this list.
tq: Find the outsider among the listed hazardous constituents.

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Constituent)
a. Lead
b. Mercury
c. Cadmium
d. Brominated flame retardants (PBBs)

List-II (Main harm or characteristic)
i. Kidney and bone damage
ii. Persistent nature and endocrine effects
iii. Nervous-system and kidney effects
iv. Brain and kidney damage; bioaccumulation in fish

Codes:
x: Lead affects the nervous system and kidneys; mercury damages the brain and kidneys and bioaccumulates in fish; cadmium damages kidneys and bones; PBBs are persistent and have endocrine effects.
tq: Start from the sure pair, especially cadmium with kidney and bone damage.

s: Improper disposal of biomedical waste and e-waste can contribute to biodiversity loss primarily because it:
o: increases the natural regeneration rate of forests
converts all pollutants into harmless nutrients
prevents the release of toxic substances into groundwater
increases soil and water toxicity and damages ecosystems
x: Improper disposal releases toxic substances into soil and water, thereby damaging ecosystems and biodiversity.
tq: Trace the cause-and-effect chain from waste disposal to ecosystem damage.

s: Which of the following is correctly arranged as the authorised e-waste recycling chain?
o: Producer → consumer → landfill → dismantler → recovered materials
Consumer → collection centre or producer take-back → authorised dismantler → authorised recycler → recovered materials
Consumer → informal hub → landfill → authorised recycler → producer take-back
Consumer → authorised recycler → collection centre → informal hub → recovered materials
x: The authorised chain begins with the consumer and collection or producer take-back, followed by dismantling, recycling and recovery of materials.
tq: Follow the material flow from generation to recovery and reject informal or disposal stages.
sec: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate action for a citizen disposing of an old electronic device?
o: Burn it to recover copper and aluminium
Mix it with municipal solid waste after removing the battery
Sell or deposit it with an authorised recycler or collection centre after wiping data
Hand it over to any informal dismantler without data removal
x: Citizens should use authorised recyclers or collection centres and wipe personal data before handing over old electronics.
tq: Apply the recommended citizen action while avoiding unsafe informal handling.
sec: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

s:
Consider the following statements about India’s e-waste recycling system:
1. E-waste should not be mixed with other waste.
2. Seelampur and Moradabad are identified as informal e-waste hubs.
3. India has 468 authorised recyclers with a combined capacity of 1.6 million tonnes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Separate handling is required; Seelampur and Moradabad are informal hubs; and CPCB data mention 468 authorised recyclers with 1.6 million tonnes of capacity.
tq: Check the operational rule, locations and capacity figure independently.
sec: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

s: What does the R2 Code of Practices primarily promote?
o: Environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling
x: R2, or Responsible Recycling, is a code of practices promoting environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
tq: Expand the abbreviation and link it to its specific sector.
sec: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

s: India’s first e-waste clinic was established at:
x: Bhopal was the location of India’s first e-waste clinic.
tq: Use the specific institutional-location association rather than an informal hub location.
sec: Recycling chain - recyclers, dismantlers, citizens, informal hubs, R2

s: India is presently described as the world’s ______ largest generator of e-waste, after China and the United States.
x: India is the third-largest e-waste generator, after China and the United States.
tq: Read the ranking together with the named countries to avoid reversing the order.
sec: E-waste magnitude - India's rank, generation, processing

s: The e-waste generation attributed to India for 2025 was approximately:
x: India’s e-waste generation was reported as approximately 2.2 million tonnes in 2025. The 3.54 lakh tonnes figure refers to e-waste collected and processed in FY 2021.
tq: Separate generation figures from collection-and-processing figures and compare their units.
sec: E-waste magnitude - India's rank, generation, processing

s: Which organisations jointly publish the Global E-waste Monitor?
x: The Global E-waste Monitor is published by the International Telecommunication Union and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.
tq: Identify the correct institutional pair instead of substituting neighbouring UN bodies.

s: The Global E-waste Monitor groups e-waste into how many categories?
x: The Global E-waste Monitor uses six categories, including cooling equipment, screens, lamps, large equipment, small equipment and IT equipment.
tq: Count the classification categories rather than the examples within them.

s: Which of the following was issued by the CPCB in response to biomedical waste generated during the COVID-19 period?
o: Global E-waste Monitor and Basel Protocol
R2 electronics recycling code and plastic treaty guidelines
COVID19BWM tracking app and COVID-19 waste guidelines
x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.
tq: Match the emergency, authority and digital tracking instrument.
sec: COVID-19 biomedical waste guidelines and tracking app

s:
Which of the following statements regarding India’s status under the Basel and Rotterdam Conventions is correct?
1. India ratified the Basel Convention in June 1992.
2. India acceded to the Rotterdam Convention in 2005.
3. India’s designated authorities for Rotterdam-related matters include the Chemicals and Fertilisers and Agriculture Ministries.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: India ratified Basel in June 1992, acceded to Rotterdam in 2005, and has designated authorities in the Chemicals and Fertilisers and Agriculture Ministries.
tq: Combine treaty dates with India-specific institutional details.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Basel Convention and India?
o: The Convention entered into force in 2004, and India acceded to it in 2005.
The Convention concerns mercury, and India ratified it in June 2005.
The Convention entered into force on 5 May 1992, and India ratified it in June 1992.
The Convention was adopted in 2013, and India ratified it in 2034.
x: The Basel Convention was adopted in 1989, entered into force on 5 May 1992, and India ratified it in June 1992.
tq: Separate adoption year, entry-into-force date and India’s ratification date.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Stockholm Convention currently includes 34 chemicals, including chlorpyrifos and PFAS.
2. The Minamata Convention concerns mercury.
3. Dental amalgam phase-out under the Minamata framework is associated with the year 2034.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The current figure given for Stockholm is 34 chemicals, including chlorpyrifos and PFAS. Minamata concerns mercury, and dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by 2034.
tq: Test the treaty’s subject together with its current chemical count and target year.

s: The global issue involved in the transboundary movement of hazardous waste refers to:
o: exchange of agricultural seeds under biodiversity agreements
movement of only biodegradable waste between rural districts
transport of clean energy equipment to developed countries
physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, often to developing countries
x: Transboundary hazardous-waste movement involves the physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, frequently to developing countries.
tq: Use the operational meaning of the term rather than an unrelated environmental transfer.

s: Which body functions as the nodal division for hazardous substances management in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
x: The Hazardous Substances Management Division (HSMD) of MoEFCC is the nodal body for hazardous substances management.
tq: Match the function with the specialised administrative division.

s: The gas responsible for the Bhopal disaster of 2–3 December 1984 was:
x: The Bhopal disaster involving Union Carbide India Ltd was caused by methyl isocyanate. More than 5,400 lives were reported lost.
tq: Distinguish the Bhopal chemical from the Visakhapatnam chemical.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Bhopal disaster in December 1984 involved methyl isocyanate. The LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam in May 2020 involved styrene vapour.
tq: Use the location–date–chemical triplet to detect swapped disaster details.

s:
With reference to the Bhopal waste cleanup reported in early 2025, consider the following statements:
1. About 337 tonnes of waste were incinerated.
2. Approximately 900 tonnes of toxic residual ash resulted.
3. The Supreme Court asked the victims’ NGO to approach the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: 337 tonnes were incinerated, about 900 tonnes of toxic residual ash remained, and the Supreme Court directed the victims’ NGO to approach the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
tq: Check the quantities, procedural direction and court involved as separate facts.

s: The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) was enacted after which major chemical disaster?
x: The EPA of 1986 was enacted after the Bhopal disaster, which occurred in December 1984.
tq: Apply the chronological cause-and-effect relationship between the disaster and legislation.

s: Which one of the following best describes PFAS, often referred to as “forever chemicals”?
o: They are biodegradable chemicals used exclusively in cement production
They persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging, and may accumulate in animal bodies
They rapidly decompose in soil and water and do not accumulate in organisms
They are radioactive substances used mainly in fluorescent lamps
x: PFAS are persistent chemicals found in drinking water, food and food packaging. They do not break down easily and can accumulate in animal bodies.
tq: Use the option that combines the defining properties and common exposure pathways.
sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

s:
With reference to PFAS, consider the following statements:
1. PFAS are widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging.
2. PFAS do not break down easily in the environment.
3. PFAS have been listed under the Stockholm Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. PFAS are persistent contaminants found in several consumer exposure pathways and are now listed under the Stockholm Convention.
tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

s: Fluorescent lamps and compact fluorescent lamps are treated as household hazardous waste primarily because they contain:
x: Fluorescent lamps and CFLs contain mercury. When broken, they can release mercury vapour into the surroundings.
tq: Identify the hazardous constituent associated with the specific consumer product.
sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the legal control associated with mercury-added products?
o: They are exempt from international environmental agreements
They are being phased out under the Minamata Convention
They are being promoted under the Stockholm Convention
They are regulated exclusively under the Basel Convention
x: Mercury-added products are being phased out under the Minamata Convention, which addresses mercury pollution and its risks.
tq: Discriminate between international conventions by matching the pollutant with the correct treaty.
sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

s: Which of the following is an example of construction and demolition waste that is generally regarded as mostly inert?
o: Mercury vapour and fluorescent lamp powder
Concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris
Used syringes, blood-soaked cotton and pathological waste
x: Construction and demolition waste is mostly inert and commonly consists of concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris.
tq: Select the option containing the characteristic material group rather than hazardous waste categories.

s: Approximately how much construction and demolition waste is generated annually, as indicated for India?
x: Construction and demolition waste generation is indicated to be about 12 million tonnes per year.
tq: Use scale comparison to distinguish the stated annual quantity from tenfold alternatives.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised reuse of construction and demolition waste?
o: Use as a substitute for all hazardous chemical treatment
x: C&D waste can be reused as recycled aggregates and in bricks and tiles. It is not a substitute for hazardous chemical treatment.
tq: Find the option outside the stated reuse pathway by separating construction applications from hazardous-waste treatment.

s: The Burari facility in Delhi is notable as:
o: India’s first fly-ash-based thermal power plant
India’s first secure landfill for hazardous waste
India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant
x: Delhi’s Burari plant is recognised as India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant.
tq: Match the named place with its distinctive facility rather than a neighbouring waste-management activity.

s: Under the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016, which of the following activities falls within the scope of construction and demolition waste management?
o: Building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline work
x: The 2016 Rules cover waste arising from building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline activities.
tq: Prefer the comprehensive scope when the rule covers multiple related activities.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. The Rules provide for collection, transport, storage and re-processing of C&D waste.
2. Bulk generators may be subject to charges.
3. Construction and demolition waste is treated as a resource.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 2016 framework covers collection, transport, storage and re-processing, permits charges on bulk generators and treats C&D waste as a resource.
tq: Test the rule through its management stages, economic provision and resource-oriented approach.

s: Which new framework is associated with the Environment (Construction and Demolition Waste Management) Rules, 2025?
o: Extended Producer Responsibility for C&D waste
A national prohibition on using recycled aggregates
A complete ban on recycling construction waste
x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for C&D waste under the 2025 rules.
tq: Identify the policy instrument directly linked with the newer rules.

s: The Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: The Hazardous Wastes (Management, Handling and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2008
x: The 2016 Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules replaced the 2008 Rules.
tq: Separate closely related rule years by identifying the earlier framework that was replaced.

s: Which one of the following correctly states a feature of the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016?
o: Import of hazardous waste for disposal is prohibited, and prevention is preferred over disposal
The Rules deal only with municipal biodegradable waste
The Rules prohibit all forms of recycling and co-processing
Hazardous waste may be imported freely for disposal without prior approval
x: The framework bans import of hazardous waste for disposal and follows a hierarchy in which prevention precedes safe disposal.
tq: Apply the waste-management hierarchy and identify the option consistent with both controls.

s: In the context of transboundary movement of hazardous waste, PIC refers to:
x: PIC means Prior Informed Consent, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.
tq: Break the abbreviation into its regulatory meaning before evaluating the options.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MSIHC Rules, 1989 — manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals
CAEPPR Rules, 1996 — insurance compensation without fault
Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 — constitution of crisis groups
Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 — regulation of fluorescent lamp manufacture
x: The MSIHC Rules, 1989 address the manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals. CAEPPR concerns crisis groups, while the Public Liability Insurance Act provides no-fault relief.
tq: Start with the sure pair and reject options that swap the functions of neighbouring legal instruments.

s: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for the establishment of:
o: Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups
x: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups for preparedness and response to chemical emergencies.
tq: Read the composition literally and avoid dropping the lower administrative levels.

s: The principal purpose of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 is to provide:
o: Compensation only after criminal conviction of the polluter
No-fault insurance cover and immediate relief to victims of hazardous-substance accidents
Insurance exclusively for transport of municipal waste
Long-term subsidies to industries using fly ash
x: The Act provides no-fault insurance cover intended to give immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.
tq: Identify the legal purpose by focusing on the beneficiary, liability basis and timing of relief.

s: Under the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025, which sequence correctly represents the time limits for assessment by the State Pollution Control Board?
o: Preliminary assessment in 30 days followed by a detailed survey in 60 days
Preliminary assessment in 90 days followed by a detailed survey in the next 90 days
Preliminary assessment in 180 days followed by a detailed survey in 30 days
Both preliminary assessment and detailed survey within 15 days
x: The SPCB is required to undertake a preliminary assessment within 90 days and a detailed survey in the subsequent 90 days.
tq: Track the sequential time periods and distinguish the first assessment from the follow-up survey.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 is correct?
o: District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared half-yearly, and the framework covers 189 hazardous chemicals
The Rules cover only radioactive substances and require monthly reports
District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared annually
The Rules apply only to municipal dumping grounds and cover 89 chemicals
x: The framework requires district half-yearly reports on suspected contaminated sites and identifies 189 hazardous chemicals.
tq: Combine the reporting frequency with the stated chemical count and reject altered figures.

s: The Fly Ash Utilisation Notification requires fly ash to be used for bricks, cement and road construction within what distance of thermal power plants?
x: The notification requires utilisation of fly ash for specified construction purposes within 300 km of thermal plants, helping prevent dumping on soil.
tq: Use the distance-based regulatory limit and distinguish it from nearer or broader alternatives.

s: Which of the following is a recognised use of fly ash in construction?
o: Treating hazardous waste without any further processing
Replacing all aggregates in every type of concrete
Making building bricks and partly replacing Portland cement in concrete
x: Fly ash can be used to make building bricks and can partly replace Portland cement in concrete.
tq: Select the option that states practical uses without introducing an absolute or exclusive claim.

s: Which principle best describes the preferred approach to hazardous-waste disposal?
o: Landfilling is the first and preferred option for all hazardous waste
Hazardous waste should always be burned in open areas
Landfill is the last resort, while co-processing in cement plants and waste exchange are preferred where suitable
All hazardous waste must be discharged into surface water after dilution
x: Landfill is considered the last resort. APPCB prefers suitable co-processing as fuel in cement plants and exchange of waste between industries.
tq: Apply the waste hierarchy and reject options based on absolute or environmentally unsafe practices.
sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

s: Which of the following correctly describes hazardous-waste management infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Two CHWTSDFs, twelve pre-processing facilities and six permitted cement units
Six CHWTSDFs, two pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units
Twelve CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and two permitted cement units
Two CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units for co-processing
x: Andhra Pradesh has two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities, six pre-processing facilities and twelve cement units permitted for co-processing.
tq: Split the numerical options into infrastructure categories and match each figure to its correct category.
sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

s: The two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDFs) in Andhra Pradesh are located at:
x: The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
tq: Use location-based recall and distinguish the named facility sites from other Andhra Pradesh cities.
sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

s: Which system is used by APEMC for tracking hazardous-waste movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Biometric tracking of every waste container
x: APEMC uses GPS tracking for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.
tq: Match the institution with the specific monitoring technology stated for it.
sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

s:
With reference to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. They came into force on 1 April 2026.
2. Household hazardous waste has been recognised as a separate ‘special care’ stream.
3. They deal exclusively with industrial hazardous waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026 and recognise household hazardous waste as a separate ‘special care’ stream. They are not confined exclusively to industrial hazardous waste.
tq: Identify the statement that wrongly narrows the scope by using the word ‘exclusively’.

s: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on:
x: The Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2025 were scheduled to come into force on 1 April 2026.
tq: Use the date-specific elimination method when several nearby dates are given.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SPSR Nellore — Operation Clean Sweep headquarters
x: Biomining of legacy waste is associated with Ongole. Anantapur is associated with a proposed 170 TPD waste-processing plant, while CHWTSDFs are located at Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
tq: Start with the sure location-activity pair and eliminate swapped places.

s: Operation Clean Sweep in Andhra Pradesh during 2026 was conducted:
o: in 113 Urban Local Bodies from 1 April to 31 May
in all villages from 23 May to 20 June
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 20 June to 23 July
in 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June
x: Operation Clean Sweep was conducted across all 123 Urban Local Bodies from 23 May to 20 June 2026 under the Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra initiative.
tq: Combine the coverage figure with the correct date range before selecting an option.

s: A municipal authority requiring an apartment complex to maintain two separate bins for waste segregation is an example associated with:
x: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) threatened to seal an apartment that did not maintain two segregation bins.
tq: Identify the implementing local authority from the nature of the municipal enforcement action.

s: Which one of the following best reflects the reported compliance position of Urban Local Bodies regarding remediation data?
o: More than 75% submit data on time
Less than 10% submit data on time
x: Only 35% of Urban Local Bodies were reported to submit timely remediation data.
tq: Watch for percentage-range traps and avoid replacing an exact figure with an approximate extreme.

s: The campaign associated with SBM-G in 2026 was:
o: Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel - Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath
x: The 2026 campaign of Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen was titled “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”. “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu” was the theme associated with June 2026.
tq: Separate the campaign title from the related monthly theme and state initiative.

s: The theme associated with June 2026 under SBM-G was:
x: The June 2026 theme was “Swachh Gaon, Surakshit Jalvayu”. It should not be confused with the broader 2026 SBM-G campaign, “Swabhav Swachhata - Sanskaar Swachhata”.
tq: Discriminate between a campaign name and a time-specific theme.

s: The Supreme Court order of 18 August 2026 regarding responsibility for waste at the threshold held that:
o: Only Urban Local Bodies are responsible for such waste
Only sanitary workers are responsible for such waste
Responsibility begins only after waste reaches a landfill
Generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for such waste
x: The Supreme Court held that generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for waste at the threshold.
tq: Reject the exclusive responsibility claim by focusing on the phrase ‘not only’.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court’s intervention in solid-waste governance:
1. The relevant order was delivered on 18 August 2026.
2. The Bench included Justice S.V.N. Bhatti.
3. On 1 September 2026, the Court pulled up the Union and State governments for not institutionalising the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The order was dated 18 August 2026, involved a Bench including Justice S.V.N. Bhatti, and the Court criticised the Union and States on 1 September 2026.
tq: Check each date, institutional actor and judicial action independently before choosing the combination.

s: Which one of the following changes has been reported in the composition of rural waste?
o: A shift from municipal waste towards only industrial hazardous waste
A shift from biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste
A complete disappearance of sanitary waste from rural areas
A shift from plastic waste towards exclusively biodegradable waste
x: Rural waste is shifting from predominantly biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste.
tq: Identify the direction of change by comparing the earlier and emerging waste categories.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported compliance position concerning Extended Producer Responsibility for plastic waste?
o: Fewer than 50% of producers comply with EPR targets
EPR targets have been withdrawn for producers
More than 90% of producers comply with EPR targets
Exactly 70% of producers comply with EPR targets
x: Fewer than 50% of producers were reported to comply with Extended Producer Responsibility targets, leading to criticism about enforceability.
tq: Distinguish the compliance percentage from the separate figure relating to informal recycling.

s:
With reference to plastic recycling and waste-pickers, consider the following statements:
1. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers.
2. The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers.
3. About 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. More than 70% of recycled plastic is handled by informal workers, NAMASTE seeks to formalise them, and approximately 15 lakh waste-pickers remain outside formal systems.
tq: Keep distinct percentages, scheme objectives and population estimates separate while evaluating the statements.

s: Which of the following is an example of ‘invisible e-waste’ commonly discarded with regular waste?
o: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories
Glass bottles, steel cans and paper cartons
Construction aggregates, fly ash and cement bags
Food scraps, garden leaves and crop residue
x: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories are examples of ‘invisible e-waste’ that may be thrown into regular waste streams.
tq: Use the category clue and select the cluster of small electronic products.

s: Weak source segregation in the reported waste-management context is indicated by segregation levels of:
x: Source segregation was reported to be under 25%, indicating weak segregation practices. This figure is distinct from the 35% of Urban Local Bodies submitting timely remediation data.
tq: Distinguish closely related percentages referring to different indicators.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the criticism surrounding the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026?
o: They were criticised on the ground that compliance was eased.
They were criticised for abolishing Extended Producer Responsibility.
They were criticised for completely banning all plastic products.
They were criticised for transferring all plastic regulation to local bodies.
x: Critics argued that the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2026 eased compliance requirements. The criticism did not amount to a complete ban or abolition of EPR.
tq: Reject extreme interpretations such as ‘completely’, ‘all’ and ‘abolishing’.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 particularly targets:
x: The Andhra Pradesh Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025–30 targets industrial hazardous waste.
tq: Match the policy with its stated target instead of selecting an over-narrow category.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the legal frameworks for which the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella?
o: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 as the only framework
x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 serves as an umbrella for frameworks including the EIA, Hazardous Waste, Coastal Regulation Zone and Contaminated Sites Rules. It is not described as an umbrella exclusively for the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
tq: Find the option that improperly uses an exclusive formulation and narrows a broader legal relationship.

s: Which of the following best explains the major institutional concern raised in relation to the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026?
o: Questions concerning federalism and administrative design
A proposal to eliminate all Urban Local Bodies
